question.text: Mr. Harish Varadarajan runs 'Kaveri SME Fund' (Cat II SME AIF). He is debating a thesis note with the IC on whether to use a long-short listed-equity overlay to hedge the SME book. Per Chapter 9 and the Cat I/II framework, what is the correct position?

answer.text: Yes, the fund can deploy 2x leverage and long-short overlays identical to Cat III.

No — long-short / market-neutral / global-macro strategies are Cat III strategies. A Cat I/II SME Fund must stick to Cat I/II-native strategies (PE equity, VC, mezzanine, growth) and cannot replicate Cat III hedge overlays.
Yes, provided the overlay is under 5% of NAV.

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III AIFs are defined by employment of complex/diverse trading strategies including leverage (up to 2x) and long-short/arbitrage. Cat I/II funds CANNOT run hedge-style strategies as core investment mandate — that would be category drift. Chapter 9's strategy list for Cat I/II is bounded to PE/VC/Debt/Infra/SSF/SVF/SME/Angel. Long-short is strictly XIX-E (future Cat III) territory. The Trap: Options A and C invent 2x leverage or size-based carve-outs that don't exist for Cat I/II. Option D is a nonsense distractor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B / XIX-E cover Cat III hedge strategies. XIX-A tests the Cat-I/II vs Cat-III distinction at distributor level. NOTE: Cat III long-short is NEVER a correct answer in XIX-D — it is only for contrast. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your SME PPM accidentally lists 'listed-equity hedging' as a strategy, SEBI will flag category drift at the 2nd quarterly submission. Scrub the PPM and the investment-policy-statement quarterly for any hedge-strategy language — only use listed-equity F&O for treasury/cash management of idle corpus, if allowed.
